intend.q: What does INTEND mean?
options: To plan or have in mind
intend.hint: INTEND means to plan something or have it in your mind.

intend.q: Which meaning goes with the word INTEND?
options: To have a plan to do it
intend.hint: If you INTEND to do it, you have a plan to do it.

intend.q: If you INTEND to build a snowman, what are you doing?
intend.hint: To INTEND is to plan. You are planning to build it.

intend.q: Which phrase explains INTEND best?
options: to have in mind to do
intend.hint: INTEND means to have something in mind to do.

intend.q: “I INTEND to read a book tonight.” What does INTEND mean here?
intend.hint: I INTEND to read means I plan to read.

intend.q: Mia says, “I INTEND to visit my aunt.” What does she mean?
intend.hint: INTEND means plan. Mia has a plan to visit.

intend.q: The word INTEND tells about something you ____.
intend.hint: When you INTEND something, you have it in mind to do.

intend.q: Which sentence gives the meaning of INTEND?
options: It means to cheer for someone.
It means to look at something closely.
It means to aim to do something.
intend.hint: INTEND means to aim or plan to do something.

intend.q: We ____ to plant flowers in the garden this spring.
intend.hint: We intend to means we plan to.

intend.q: I ____ to ask my teacher for help with math.
intend.hint: I intend to ask means I plan to ask.

intend.q: Do you ____ to wear your red coat today?
intend.hint: Intend means plan. Do you plan to wear it?

intend.q: Tom does not ____ to be late for the bus.
intend.hint: Tom has no plan to be late, so he does not intend it.

intend.q: My sister and I ____ to bake cookies on Saturday.
intend.hint: We plan to bake, so we intend to bake.

intend.q: “What do you ____ to do at recess?” asked Ben.
intend.hint: Ben asks what you plan to do.

intend.q: Lena ____ to bring a gift, but she forgot it at home.
intend.hint: Lena had a plan to bring it. She intended to.

intend.q: Grandpa ____ to teach me how to fish this summer.
intend.hint: Grandpa has a plan to teach me. He intends to.

intend.q: The twins ____ to finish their project before dinner.
intend.hint: The twins plan to finish, so they intend to.

intend.q: We ____ to win the race, so we trained every day.
intend.hint: We had a plan to win. We intend to win.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: I INTEND to walk the dog after lunch.
I INTEND the dog a big loud bark.
The dog INTEND on my red blanket.
intend.hint: INTEND goes with a plan: I INTEND to walk the dog.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: Sara INTENDS her book a nice blue.
Sara INTENDS to finish her book this week.
This book INTENDS under the table.
intend.hint: Sara has a plan to finish her book.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: The zoo INTEND us a big cold.
We INTEND to visit the zoo on Friday.
Friday INTEND the zoo very tall.
intend.hint: We INTEND to visit means we plan to visit.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: Did you INTEND my pencil quickly?
My pencil INTEND the table to eat.
Did you INTEND to take my pencil?
intend.hint: Did you INTEND to means: did you plan to?

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: Max INTENDED to say sorry to his friend.
Max INTENDED sorry a new, big box.
His friend INTENDED the sorry floor.
intend.hint: Max planned to say sorry, so he INTENDED to.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: They INTEND the fence a green sleep.
The paint INTEND to eat the fence.
They INTEND to paint the fence green.
intend.hint: They have a plan to paint the fence.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: I do not INTEND to miss the school play.
I do not INTEND the school play wet.
The play does INTEND me to missing.
intend.hint: I do not INTEND to miss means I do not plan to miss it.

intend.q: Which sentence uses INTEND correctly?
options: Ella INTENDS a tree for her loud lunch.
Ella INTENDS to plant a tree for Earth Day.
The tree INTENDS Ella on Earth Day.
intend.hint: Ella has a plan to plant a tree.

intend.q: Which word is closest in meaning to INTEND?
intend.hint: INTEND and plan mean almost the same.

intend.q: Which words mean almost the same as INTEND?
intend.hint: To aim to do something is to INTEND it.

intend.q: “I INTEND to go” is most like “I ____ to go.”
intend.hint: I plan to go means I INTEND to go.

intend.q: Which word can take the place of INTEND? “We INTEND to camp.”
intend.hint: We plan to camp means the same thing.

intend.q: Which pair of words are synonyms?
intend.hint: INTEND and plan both mean to have in mind to do.

intend.q: Which is the best match for INTEND?
intend.hint: To INTEND is to mean to do something.

intend.q: Which is the opposite of INTEND?
intend.hint: If you INTEND, you plan. The opposite is having no plan.

intend.q: Sam INTENDS to join the club. Which sentence says the opposite?
options: Sam has no plan to join the club.
Sam has a plan to join the club.
Sam is aiming to join the club.
intend.hint: The opposite of having a plan is having no plan.

intend.q: Which person does NOT INTEND to go to the party?
options: Kim, who has no plan to go
intend.hint: Kim has no plan to go, so she does not INTEND to.

intend.q: Which is the opposite of “I INTEND to try”?
options: I have no plan to try.
intend.hint: INTEND means to plan, so the opposite is no plan.

intend.q: Which choice is the opposite of having a plan to do something?
options: to have no plan at all
intend.hint: To INTEND is to plan or have in mind; having no plan is the opposite.

intend.q: Which sentence is the opposite of “Leo INTENDS to run in the race”?
options: Leo aims to run in the race.
Leo will run in the race soon.
Leo has no plan to run in the race.
intend.hint: INTENDS means has a plan. The opposite is no plan.

intend.q: Ravi tells his coach, “I INTEND to practice free throws every day.” What is Ravi sharing?
intend.hint: INTEND means plan, so Ravi is sharing his plan.

intend.q: Grandma smells apple pie and says, “I INTEND to have two pieces!” What does she mean?
intend.hint: INTEND means plan. Grandma plans to have two pieces.

intend.q: A dog digs by the fence. Kai says, “I think he INTENDS to get out.” What does Kai think?
intend.hint: Kai thinks the dog has a plan to get out.

intend.q: On the first day of school, Zoe says she INTENDS to make a new friend. What is Zoe doing?
intend.hint: Zoe has a plan to make a friend.

intend.q: Dad says, “We INTEND to put up holiday lights on Saturday.” What does that tell you?
options: They plan to do it Saturday.
intend.hint: INTEND means plan. The lights are planned for Saturday.

intend.q: Nina holds a board game and says, “I INTEND to win this time!” What does this show?
options: She has it in mind to win.
intend.hint: INTEND means to have in mind. Nina plans to win.

intend.q: A bird gathers sticks in a tree. Which sentence shows the bird INTENDS to build a nest?
options: The bird is afraid of the sticks.
The bird has a plan to make a nest.
The bird is flying to the sea.
intend.hint: Gathering sticks fits a plan to build a nest.

intend.q: Omar says, “I INTEND to clean my room after lunch.” What should Omar do after lunch?
intend.hint: INTEND means plan. Omar plans to clean his room.

intend.q: Is INTEND a noun or a verb?
intend.hint: INTEND is a verb. You INTEND to do something.

intend.q: Which is the past tense of INTEND?
intend.hint: Add -ed to make the past tense: intended.

intend.q: Pick the form that fits: Pablo ____ to help.
intend.hint: With Pablo, use the verb intends. Intention is a noun.

intend.q: Which word names the plan or aim itself?
intend.hint: Intention is the noun. It names a plan or aim.

intention.q: What does INTENTION mean?
intention.hint: INTENTION means an aim, a plan, or a purpose.

intention.q: Which is the best meaning of INTENTION?
intention.hint: Your INTENTION is what you plan or aim to do.

intention.q: Your INTENTION is the thing you ____.
intention.hint: An INTENTION is an aim or plan.

intention.q: “My INTENTION was to help.” What does INTENTION mean here?
intention.hint: My plan was to help. INTENTION means plan.

intention.q: Which words mean the same as INTENTION?
intention.hint: INTENTION means a plan or a purpose.

intention.q: If you tell a friend your INTENTION, you are sharing your ____.
intention.hint: Your INTENTION is your plan.

intention.q: Which sentence explains the word INTENTION?
options: It is a cheer from a crowd.
It is the purpose you have in mind.
It is a very small snack.
intention.hint: An INTENTION is a purpose you have in mind.

intention.q: INTENTION is a word for a ____.
intention.hint: INTENTION means a plan or an aim.

intention.q: Her ____ was to make her grandma smile.
intention.hint: Her aim was to make Grandma smile. That is her intention.

intention.q: It was never my ____ to hurt your feelings.
intention.hint: It was never my plan or purpose to hurt you.

intention.q: What is your ____ for the science fair?
intention.hint: Intention means plan. What is your plan?

intention.q: Jake’s good ____ was to share his snack.
intention.hint: Jake’s purpose was a kind one. That is his intention.

intention.q: The team’s ____ is to win the cup.
intention.hint: The team’s aim is to win. That is its intention.

intention.q: He had the best of ____ when he baked the cake.
intention.hint: Good intentions means good plans or purposes.

intention.q: Our ____ was to arrive early, but the bus was late.
intention.hint: Our plan was to arrive early. That was our intention.

intention.q: Nora carried the bags with the ____ of helping.
intention.hint: Nora’s purpose was to help. That is her intention.

intention.q: The ____ behind the poster was to teach kids to recycle.
intention.hint: The aim behind the poster was to teach. That is the intention.

intention.q: Ana has no ____ of quitting the choir.
intention.hint: Ana has no plan to quit. She has no intention.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: I INTENTION ten books to the sky.
Ten books INTENTION me very loud.
My INTENTION is to read ten books this year.
intention.hint: INTENTION is a noun: my plan is to read ten books.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: She INTENTION to be rude quickly.
Her INTENTION ran fast to the door.
It was never her INTENTION to be rude.
intention.hint: Her plan was never to be rude. That is her INTENTION.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: What is your INTENTION for the school fair?
The school fair INTENTION very loudly.
Please INTENTION me the school fair.
intention.hint: What is your INTENTION asks about your plan.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: We INTENTION the park by the lake.
Our INTENTION was to clean the park.
The park INTENTION us to clean.
intention.hint: Our plan was to clean the park.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: He had good INTENTIONS when he fed the fish.
He INTENTIONS the fish a snack.
The fish had INTENTIONED him a net.
intention.hint: Good INTENTIONS are kind plans or purposes.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: Her INTENTION was to surprise her mom with a card.
Her mom INTENTION a surprise card to eat.
Her card INTENTION was blue to mom.
intention.hint: Her purpose was to surprise her mom.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: The coach INTENTION the team a ball.
The team INTENTION the coach loud.
The coach explained his INTENTION to the team.
intention.hint: The coach told the team his plan, his INTENTION.

intention.q: Which sentence uses INTENTION correctly?
options: I have no INTENTION my project on the shelf.
I INTENTION no giving up of project.
I have no INTENTION of giving up on my project.
intention.hint: No INTENTION of giving up means no plan to give up.

intention.q: Which word is closest in meaning to INTENTION?
intention.hint: INTENTION and purpose mean almost the same.

intention.q: Which word is a synonym for INTENTION?
intention.hint: An aim is the same as an INTENTION.

intention.q: INTENTION is most like which word?
intention.hint: An INTENTION is a plan.

intention.q: Which word could replace INTENTION? “Her INTENTION was to win.”
intention.hint: Her goal was to win. Goal and INTENTION are alike.

intention.q: Which pair of words has almost the same meaning?
intention.hint: INTENTION and purpose both mean a plan or aim.

intention.q: Choose the closest match for INTENTION.
intention.hint: Your INTENTION is what you mean to do.

intention.q: Which word is the opposite of INTENTION?
intention.hint: An accident happens with no plan, the opposite of an INTENTION.

intention.q: Which happens WITHOUT an INTENTION?
intention.hint: An accident has no plan or INTENTION behind it.

intention.q: Which is the opposite of doing something with INTENTION?
intention.hint: With INTENTION means on purpose. The opposite is by accident.

intention.q: Kit knocked over the paint, but it was NOT her intention. How did it happen?
intention.hint: No INTENTION means no plan, so it was an accident.

intention.q: Which is closest to the OPPOSITE of INTENTION?
intention.hint: An INTENTION has a plan. Chance has none.

intention.q: Which idea is the opposite of having an INTENTION?
intention.hint: INTENTION means plan, so no plan is the opposite.

intention.q: Ben says his INTENTION is to be a vet one day. What is Ben telling you?
intention.hint: INTENTION means plan or aim. Ben shares his plan.

intention.q: Priya dropped a cup. “It was not my INTENTION!” she said. What does she mean?
options: She did not mean to do it.
intention.hint: No INTENTION means she did not plan it.

intention.q: At the holiday party, Uncle Jo says, “My INTENTION is to sing three songs.” What is he sharing?
intention.hint: INTENTION means plan. Uncle Jo plans to sing.

intention.q: Coach asks, “What is your INTENTION for Saturday’s game?” What is she asking?
intention.hint: She asks about your plan for the game.

intention.q: A puppy chews a shoe. Lina says, “His INTENTION was only to play.” What is she saying?
intention.hint: INTENTION means purpose. His purpose was to play.

intention.q: Eli’s INTENTION was to win the spelling bee, so he studied each night. What did Eli have?
intention.hint: INTENTION means plan or aim. Eli had a goal.

intention.q: Maya saves coins in a jar. Her INTENTION is to buy a kite. Why does she save?
intention.hint: Her aim, her INTENTION, is to buy a kite.

intention.q: Dad says his INTENTION is to make pancakes on Sunday. What will Dad do?
intention.hint: INTENTION means plan. Dad plans to make pancakes.

intention.q: Is INTENTION a noun or a verb?
intention.hint: INTENTION is a noun. It names a plan or aim.

intention.q: Which word is the verb that goes with INTENTION?
intention.hint: Intend is the verb. Intention is the noun.

intention.q: Pick the word that fits: It was my ____ to help.
intention.hint: After “my” we need a noun, so use intention.

intention.q: Which sentence uses the plural form, INTENTIONS?
options: Her INTENTIONS were good and kind.
intention.hint: INTENTIONS is plural. It means more than one plan or aim.
